data.title: NSA lost access to Mythos amid Anthropic dispute
data.author: thm
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NSA失去Anthropic的Mythos模型访问权限引发的争议

不同观点：
• **怀疑论者**：认为NSA不可能真正失去访问权限，Anthropic内部很可能有情报机构的线人（dofm, AustinDev），NSA可以随时强制获取模型权重（sometimelurker, AustinDev）

• **营销炒作批评者**：认为整个事件是PR战和营销噱头（medlazik, dofm），将Mythos描述得过于危险是为了提升Anthropic的市场地位，类似于之前AI行业的各种夸大宣传

• **安全能力关注者**：对Mythos的实际能力存在疑虑，有人指出它能在数小时内攻破机密系统（chasil引用），也有人认为配合IDA Pro等工具可突破安全防护（teravor）

• **讽刺/幽默派**：嘲讽NSA失去访问权限的荒谬性（Woodi），或对整个情况表示不屑（charcircuit, zb3明确表示不希望NSA获得访问权限）

• **双重标准批评**：指出政府和Anthropic的矛盾立场——政府既视模型为供应链风险又要求使用，Anthropic既称模型危险如核武器又公开发布（jawiggins）

补充讨论：有评论提及当前政府对情报机构的裁员可能进一步削弱美国情报能力（ck2）

data.title: GitHub shouldn't be a dependency for publishing Rust on crates.io
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust 的 Cargo 包管理系统过度依赖 GitHub 的问题及解决方案

不同观点：
• **官方进展派**：RFC 已合并，实现工作已启动。这是志愿者驱动的项目，枯燥任务需要资金和审查者支持。解耦工作量大且复杂，类似"火车行驶中重建轨道"，目前优先级不高但官方有路线图欢迎贡献（epage, vsgherzi, ameliaquining）

• **强硬反对派**：GitHub 和 NPM 都是微软旗下，是"最严重的负债"。任何可能随意封禁用户的单点故障都不应成为开源项目的看门人，必须彻底移除依赖（zombot, Animats, dboreham）

• **供应链安全派**：Cargo 与 npm、PyPI 风险类似——安装包意味着信任外部代码。与其指责 GitHub，不如关注如何加固生态系统（r2vcap）

• **历史context派**：Cargo 绑定 GitHub 是在其"开源乌托邦"形象时期，现在依赖已深度嵌入，回滚极其困难（linzhangrun）

• **他山之石派**：Go 语言处理得较好，可从 GitHub URL 透明导入，也支持自托管；PHP 的 Packagist 强制从源仓库打包，防止制品与源码不一致（lorecore, mikey_p）

补充讨论：有人吐槽"十年了还没解决"，也有人调侃"万一 GitHub 宕机怎么办"

data.title: How the Fifth Lateran Council unlocked financial theory
data.author: momentmaker
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述中世纪经济理论如何影响现实。方济各会修士奥利维在13世纪提出机会成本和风险理论,为有息贷款的合理性奠定基础。15世纪方济各会支持Monte di Pietà(慈善信贷机构)向穷人提供低息抵押贷款,用利息支付运营成本。多明我会反对任何形式的收息。1515年教皇利奥十世在拉特兰会议上支持方济各会,正式认可Monte di Pietà的做法,承认适当限制下的利息是管理费用的合理补偿,标志着天主教会对高利贷禁令的重要松动。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：天主教高利贷理论和经济哲学的演变

不同观点：
• **天主教高利贷的定义**（dmenj）：中世纪语境下的高利贷指的是在mutuum贷款（可消耗品借贷合同）中获取利润，适用于所有可替代物品而非仅限金钱。核心是区分"内在权利"（贷款本身带来利润权，这是不道德的）和"外在权利"（因贷款产生的外部成本可获补偿，如机会成本lucrum cessans和损失damnum emergens）。文中Monti案例属于外在权利中的行政成本补偿，而非营利。

• **现代法律定义的转变**（hvs）：当代"高利贷"一词的法律含义已从"任何利息"演变为"超过法定上限的利息收费"，反映了社会对借贷利息态度的根本性转变。

• **经济哲学的时代差异**（Schlagbohrer）：亚当·斯密（1776年）观察的是前工业时代的原材料经济，而马克思（1848年）面对的是工业化后注重增值活动的经济体系。不同经济结构催生了不同的社会后果和哲学思想。推荐David Harvey对《资本论》的现代解读，认为理解马克思有助于成为更好的资本家。

补充讨论：评论展现了从宗教道德框架到法律框架，再到经济哲学演变的历史脉络，体现了人类对"借贷获利"这一行为理解的深刻变化。

48611940.article_content:
Advances in medieval economic theory had greater real-world consequences than many know. Among economists, Joseph Schumpeter’s economic history mostly starts economic theory with the Salamancans. Tyler Cowen in
The Marginal Revolution
states that the advances of the Salamanca school remained largely ignored, and the connection between economic theory and practice was non-existent until 1776, when Adam Smith made a treatment of economics so systematic that economics became a field in its own right. And even still, the key insights of demand, supply, and marginal slopes took a century more, until Walras and Jevons.
Yet within finance, academic theory had real-world consequences, starting of course with the theory of usury.
The moral theory of usury grew in import throughout the first seven centuries of Christianity, but it was a single moral theory, not an economic one. The idea was that interest on loans was a way to get money without work; it was not only a form of sloth, but also a pure transfer from the borrower to the lender. The practice was much maligned and often condemned by the Catholic Church. Perhaps in a Malthusian world this makes sense, but nonetheless loans were frequently necessary to overcome difficulties, and future flows of cash and crop are always tempting to mortgage. The Jewish ghettoed underclass met the demand of kings for cash now and charged interest. They were resented and abused, but useful.
Joel Kaye has shown that the thirteenth-century expansion of trade helped spur refinement of scholastic economic theory, especially for Franciscans, whose views and practices of poverty were contentious. Two very important theories of finance had been developed by the great Franciscan Peter John Olivi in the late thirteenth century: opportunity cost and risk. According to Olivi, it was because of opportunity cost and risk that merchants justly can make profits on arbitrage, seek modest returns on a loan, and charge a range of prices based on market conditions. It took the radical poverty of the Franciscans to see with fresh eyes the value to society provided by merchants and trade!
These theories provided groundwork for the idea that interest-bearing loans could be socially valuable rather than merely extractive. Another Franciscan, Bernardino da Feltre, took up the argument, extended it, and openly supported low-interest lending to the poor. He helped Pavia set up a Monte in the fifteenth century. The Monte was a collateralized loan service initially funded by donations. Poor and middle-class people could pawn an item in exchange for a loan. What made this controversial was that the one-year loan would bear interest between 2 and 15% per year to pay for the stewards of the fund. Were profits on a loan morally legitimate if they only paid for the management of the loan? In Leo X’s formulation the interest gained was given a list of legal uses, all of which were meant to indicate that loan services should have zero producer surplus. At first, only the expense of running the fund was an approved use of the interest, and any additional profits were to help the poor. However, the notion of just remuneration to the Monte expanded to include both opportunity cost and risk. And at the same time, in practice, the notion of “help the poor” expanded — as did who could deposit funds in the Monte.
While the Franciscans supported a limited form of lending at interest in charitable circumstances, the Dominicans took the other side of the debate. The Dominicans thought the loosening of the purse was also a loosening of morals. For how could a person charge interest in any circumstance without opening the door to justifying interest in many circumstances? It is not how the interest is used that makes it just or unjust. It is the act itself: as soon as you’ve charged interest, no matter how noble the cause the interest is put to, you’ve stolen from the laborer as an idle lender. The ongoing dispute was on the docket to be resolved at the Fifth Lateran Council.
Painting of St. Dominic (on left) and St. Francis by Angelo Lion (1597-1621)
At that council in 1515 Franciscan financial reasoning won. The Monti di Pietà were sanctioned by Pope Leo X. The 1515 document
Inter multiplices
gave full license to the practice. He understood that the Monti, properly restricted, helped and did not harm, and the payment in interest was a just fee for the administration of the program.
“We commend the zeal for justice displayed by the former group, which desires to prevent the opening up of the chasm of usury, as well as the love of piety and truth shown by the latter group, which wishes to aid the poor, and indeed the earnestness of both sides. data.title: Pondering routing more of my traffic via nodes outside the UK
data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary: 作者因担忧英国网络安全政策方向，正考虑将流量路由至英国境外节点。英国政府以"网络安全"为名推出的政策威胁到言论自由和隐私权，包括禁止16岁以下用户使用社交媒体（可能导致广泛的身份验证）、《网络安全法》引发的网站屏蔽英国IP、ISP实施DNS封锁、以及越来越多网站屏蔽Tor流量。作者首次考虑在英国境外部署WireGuard节点、SOCKS代理或DNS服务器来维持网络访问自由，认为英国网络审查已达到令人遗憾的地步，这种需求本身就像反乌托邦科幻小说的情节。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国网络审查和年龄验证政策下，技术人员如何通过VPN、代理等方式绕过限制，以及对政府监管的不同态度。

不同观点：

• **技术规避派**：详细分享绕过审查的技术方案（WireGuard、Mullvad VPN、自建代理、递归DNS等），强调"数据由我掌控"。认为通过策略路由、流量混淆等手段可维持网络访问自由。

• **悲观现实派**：认为VPN/Tor并非真正解决方案，政府可轻易封禁VPN IP段、指纹识别WireGuard流量，最终可能立法禁止VPN使用。指出唯一出路是更换政党，但几乎所有政党都支持审查。

• **阴谋论视角**：认为"保护儿童"是幌子，真实目的是强制身份验证、消除网络匿名性。引用新西兰清真寺袭击后的全球审查协同，怀疑存在国际势力推动（如"Christchurch Call"）。担心最终演变为深度包检测和完全监控。

• **支持监管派**：质疑将儿童称为"16岁以下人群"的表述，认为英国表达自由渠道充足，隐私不等于匿名。只要不帮助儿童大规模规避年龄门槛，个人使用VPN无妨。

补充讨论：部分人对工党政策困惑，认为其试图"比保守党更保守"以迎合《每日邮报》读者群；有人彻底放弃互联网，认为它已不复20年前的开放状态。

48614309.article_content:
Pondering routing more of my traffic via nodes outside the UK because of the direction of UK online safety policy
Published on:
2026-06-20 21:00:07
by
Neil Brown
Some of the UK governmentâs policy announcements around the Internet
- and, in particular, social media and VPNs - are downright concerning
me at the moment.
In the name of âonline safetyâ, the fundamental rights of both
freedom of expression and privacy appear to be under imminent
threat.
I have concerns which go beyond our shores - mostly stemming from
Google, frankly - but the UK legislative / policy issues are bothering
me especially at the moment.
I value my ability to read, learn, and communicate almost without
borders. I donât like signing up to websites or newsletters (I prefer
RSS), I donât like storing my data on other peopleâs computers, and Iâve
certainly no wish to prove my age or identity outside core government
services.
The current proposal to ban people under 16 - who also have the
rights to freedom of expression and privacy - from some (as yet not
fully delineated) social media services is likely to result in
wide-spread verification.
While I am unlikely to be affected directly - although it would
depend on the definition of âsocial mediaâ - I anticipate that more
websites will simply choose to block traffic from UK IP addresses,
especially if UK-originated traffic does not matter a huge amount to
them.
I am already seeing this as a consequence of the Online Safety Act,
and I expect any future UK laws in this area to exacerbate that.
I also anticipate that we will soon see the first court-ordered
blocking injunctions under the Online Safety Act, when the fines issued
by Ofcom against some website providers (so far, most quite niche porn
sites, as far as I can tell, plus a âsuicide discussion forumâ) go
unpaid and the âcompliance issuesâ which Ofcom has identified go
unresolved.
Some - many - UK ISPs have already implemented, and carry out, DNS
blocking, both for mandatory and non-mandatory reasons. Mine - A&A -
is probably one of the outliers, with no blocking save for the mandatory
sanctions-related requirements.
In any case, so far, since I run my own recursive DNS infrastructure,
I have not been affected.
I use Tor quite a lot, but Iâve seen an increase - sure, a small
increase, but an increase nevertheless - of sites which are blocking Tor
traffic.
And so, for the first time, I am considering locating something
(perhaps a WireGuard node, or a SOCKS proxy, or a recursive DNS server /
DNS proxy, or perhaps all of them) somewhere on the Internet outside the
UK, so that I can route some traffic through that, as needed, to
maintain my access to the web.
Honestly, it seems such a shame to me, that UK Internet censorship
should reach such a place, but there we go.
I have not decided exactly what I might do, or exactly how, or where,
I might do it, but it is far more attractive to me now that it has been
ever before, in all the 30ish years that Iâve been online.
To me, the need to even contemplate this kind of thing is the stuff
of dystopian sci-fi.
And yet here I find myself.

补充讨论：部分人对工党政策困惑，认为其试图"比保守党更保守"以迎合《每日邮报》读者群；有人彻底放弃互联网，认为它已不复20年前的开放状态。

data.article_summary: 52赫兹鲸是一头在北太平洋发出异常频率叫声的神秘鲸鱼。它以52赫兹频率鸣叫，远高于蓝鲸（10-39赫兹）和长须鲸（20赫兹）。自1989年首次被声呐探测到以来，每年都能监测到它的叫声，但从未被目击过。它独自迁徙于阿留申群岛至加州海岸之间，叫声独特且无同类回应，因此被称为"世界上最孤独的鲸鱼"。科学家无法确定其物种，推测可能是畸形或杂交蓝鲸。2010年后偶尔发现第二头52赫兹鲸的录音。这一现象引发了多部纪录片和动画短片的创作。

48665093.article_content:
From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Whale who calls at unusual frequency
"52 Hertz" redirects here. For the Iranian short film, see
52 Hertz (film)
.
A
spectrogram
of the 52-hertz signal
The
52-hertz whale
, colloquially referred to as
52 Blue
, is an individual
whale
of unidentified species that
calls
at the unusual frequency of 52
hertz
in the north Pacific Ocean between Aleutian and Kodiak Islands to the California coast. The whale itself has never been sighted: it has only been heard via
hydrophones
, but its call has been detected since the late 1980s in a pattern that matches the migration of the
blue whale
and the
fin whale
. Those species call at 10 to 39 Hz and 20 Hz respectively. Described as the "world's loneliest whale", it appeared to be the only individual emitting a whale call at this frequency. However, recordings of a second 52-hertz whale, heard elsewhere at the same time, have been sporadically found since 2010.
The 52 Hz frequency is roughly equivalent to the musical note G
#
1
, which is the 12th lowest key on a standard 88-key
piano
keyboard, or the 4th finger position on the lowest string (E
1
) of a
double bass
.
Characteristics
[
edit
]
The 52-hertz whale
The signal was recorded in the northeast Pacific. It has been sped up ten times, raising the pitch to 520 Hz (C
5
).
Problems playing this file? See
media help
.
The sonic signature is that of a whale, albeit at a unique frequency. The call patterns resemble neither
blue
nor
fin whales
, being much higher in frequency, shorter, and more frequent.
[
1
]
Blue whales usually vocalize at 10–39 Hz,
[
2
]
fin whales at 20 Hz.
[
3
]
The calls of this whale are highly variable in their pattern of repetition, duration, and sequence, although they are easily identifiable due to their frequency and characteristic clustering.
[
4
]
The calls deepened slightly to around 50 hertz by 2004, consistent with the expectations of a maturing whale.
[
5
]
The migration track of the 52-hertz whale is unrelated to the presence or movement of other whale species.
[
6
]
Its movements have been somewhat similar to that of blue whales, but its timing has been more like that of fin whales.
[
4
]
It is detected in the
Pacific Ocean
every year beginning in August and remaining through December, and moves out of range of the hydrophones in January–February. It travels as far north as the
Aleutian
and
Kodiak Islands
, and as far south as the
California
coast, swimming between 30 and 70 km (20 and 40 mi) each day. Its recorded distance traveled per season has ranged from a low of 708 km (440 mi) to a high of 11,062 km (6,874 mi) in 2002–03.
[
7
]
Scientists at the
Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution
have been unable to identify the species of the whale. They speculate that it could be
malformed
or a
blue whale
hybrid
.
[
6
]
The research team is often contacted by deaf people who wonder whether the whale might also be deaf.
[
8
]
Whatever biological cause underlies its unusually high-frequency voice does not seem to be detrimental to its survival. The whale's survival and apparent maturity indicate it is probably healthy. Still, its call is the only one of its kind detected anywhere and there is only one such source per season.
[
7
]
Because of this, the animal has been called the loneliest whale in the world.
[
1
]
[
9
]
[
10
]
Nevertheless, calls picked up by a sensor in California in 2010 suggest that there may be more than one whale calling at 52 Hz.
[
11
]
History
[
edit
]
Approximate map of the 52-hertz whale's migration range
The 52-hertz whale was discovered by a team from the
Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution
. Its call was first detected in 1989, then again in 1990 and 1991.
[
7
]
In 1992, following the end of the
Cold War
, the
U.S. Navy
partially declassified the recordings and technical specifications of its
SOSUS
anti-submarine hydrophone arrays, and it made SOSUS available for oceanographic research.
[
4
]
[
6
]
As of 2014
[update]
, the whale had been detected every year since.
[
12
]
In media
[
edit
]
Films
[
edit
]
The Loneliest
, a short
mockumentary
film about two women searching for the loneliest whale, was made by Lilian T. Mehrel with support from an
Alfred P. Sloan Foundation
production grant.
[
13
]
The animated short film
The Phantom 52
premiered at the
Sundance Film Festival
in January 2019. The film was written and directed by
Geoff Marslett
, and stars
Tom Skerritt
as the loneliest whale.
[
14
]
The feature-length documentary
The Loneliest Whale: The Search for 52
, directed by Joshua Zeman, the director of
Cropsey
, and executive producers
Leonardo DiCaprio
and
Adrian Grenier
, was commercially released by
Bleecker Street
on July 9, 2021.
[
15
]
The film follows Zeman and a group of five scientists and oceanographers on a quest to find the whale off the coast of California. Funded through a
Kickstarter
campaign,
[
16
]
the film received generally positive reviews among critics, holding an approval rating of 86% based on 35 review

data.title: Mixing Visual and Textual Code
data.author: doppioandante
data.article_summary: 这篇论文介绍了Hybrid ClojureScript，一种混合编程语言，允许开发者在代码中同时使用文本和可视化语法来表达特定领域的几何概念。该语言支持程序员添加可视化交互语法并将其嵌入到程序文本中，在增强的混合IDE中显示为可交互的mini-GUI界面，而在普通IDE中则显示为文本形式。这种设计将视觉语法和文本语法置于平等地位，作为可组合的语言扩展，同时保留了程序的静态推理能力，不会打断程序员的正常工作流程。论文论证了这种可扩展机制的必要性和采用可行性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于在源代码中混合文本与视觉元素（图像、图表等）的可行性和历史实践

不同观点：
• **技术上可行但实践困难**（kitd, donaldihunter）：Eclipse插件可以从注释生成状态图，但在文本编辑器中维护ASCII图表极其痛苦；视觉语言在并发开发、版本控制、diff/merge方面存在根本性障碍，XML序列化也难以处理
• **已有成功先例**（cml123, Izkata）：TempleOS的DolDoc格式实现了代码与精灵图的无缝混合；SikuliX的IDE用图像替换Python函数参数，提供直接的图像操作功能
• **跨上下文集成挑战**（doctorhandshake）：在TouchDesigner中，节点与Python脚本间的操作顺序、职责分配和状态存储仍是未解决的难题
• **展示不足**（Garlef）：作者应该用浏览器演示实际程序来更好地推广这个想法
• **技术已商业化**（conartist6）：暗示类似技术可能已在学术论文发表前实现商业应用

补充讨论：多位评论者提到相关项目（Polytope、Ink & Switch），并表达希望将此方法应用于3D CAD等领域。有人质疑为何现有IDE的AST未被充分利用来渲染抽象代码和系统。

Title:
Mixing Visual and Textual Code
Authors:
Leif Andersen
,
Michael Ballantyne
,
Cameron Moy
,
Matthias Felleisen
,
Stephen Chang
View a PDF of the paper titled Mixing Visual and Textual Code, by Leif Andersen and 4 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
The dominant programming languages support nothing but linear text to express domain-specific geometric ideas. What is needed are hybrid languages that allow developers to create visual syntactic constructs so that they can express their ideas with a mix of textual and visual syntax tailored to an application domain. This mix must put the two kinds of syntax on equal footing and, just as importantly, the extended language must not disrupt a programmer's typical workflow. This means that any new visual syntax should be a proper language extension that is composable with other language features. Furthermore, the extensions should also preserve static reasoning about the program. This paper presents Hybrid ClojureScript the first such hybrid programming language. Hybrid ClojureScript allows programmers to add visual interactive syntax and to embed instances of this syntax within a program's text. An enhanced hybrid IDE can then display these embedded instances as mini-GUIs that programmers interact with, while other IDEs will show a textual representation of the syntax. The paper argues the necessity of such an extensibility mechanism, demonstrates the adoptability of the design, and discusses what might be needed to use the design in other languages.

48667560.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于在源代码中混合文本与视觉元素（图像、图表等）的可行性和历史实践

不同观点：
• **技术上可行但实践困难**（kitd, donaldihunter）：Eclipse插件可以从注释生成状态图，但在文本编辑器中维护ASCII图表极其痛苦；视觉语言在并发开发、版本控制、diff/merge方面存在根本性障碍，XML序列化也难以处理
• **已有成功先例**（cml123, Izkata）：TempleOS的DolDoc格式实现了代码与精灵图的无缝混合；SikuliX的IDE用图像替换Python函数参数，提供直接的图像操作功能
• **跨上下文集成挑战**（doctorhandshake）：在TouchDesigner中，节点与Python脚本间的操作顺序、职责分配和状态存储仍是未解决的难题
• **展示不足**（Garlef）：作者应该用浏览器演示实际程序来更好地推广这个想法
• **技术已商业化**（conartist6）：暗示类似技术可能已在学术论文发表前实现商业应用

补充讨论：多位评论者提到相关项目（Polytope、Ink & Switch），并表达希望将此方法应用于3D CAD等领域。有人质疑为何现有IDE的AST未被充分利用来渲染抽象代码和系统。

Currently, I’m in the midst of writing
a big post about the roots of web forums, but I hit on an aside weird enough that I decided to stop writing that and work on a separate post. Because I think it actually explains a lot about the way people use the internet.
Essentially, here’s the deal. Around 1995 or so, a high schooler named
Matt Wright
decided to launch a website that shared some basic website tools that he programmed. Many of these were dead-simple, things like contact forms, guestbooks, and web counters. One in particular, WWWBoard, became a massive hit, becoming one of the first widely used web forum apps on the internet.
The copyright notice for WWWBoard, Wright’s widely used forum-hosting software.
The site Wright built,
Matt’s Script Archive
, unwittingly helped to highlight the divergence between how normal people think about software, and the developer’s perspective.
Wright, and others like him, hit upon an obvious need. Regular people found these scripts, ran them, and suddenly had forums, counters, and contact forms. They got the job done. But programmers who weren’t in high school and weren’t so wet behind the ears looked aghast at what Wright had done: He had spread poorly designed, but widely used software across the internet. This software was packed with security issues, but worst of all, it wasn’t really getting updated all that much.
How serious are the security issues? Well,
a look at OpenCVE
points out some very serious problems that range from bugs that emerged from massive exposure to some questionable design decisions. (Keeping an encrypted password file in the root? Making it possible to grab env variables via a URL? Not smart!)
One exploit in particular, affecting Wright’s textcounter tool, stands out among the list:
CVE-1999-1479
, with a score of 10.0 critical, effectively allows exploiters to execute code on the server as root.
You mean Matt has a script archive? Let’s have the Perl pros take a turn.
This state of affairs got serious enough that a competing website, called
nms
, essentially was launched to replace Matt’s buggy scripts with drop-in versions aren’t full of security exploits from bad coding. Their POV:
The problem is that the scripts in Matt’s Script Archive aren’t very good. The scripts are well known amongst the Perl community to be badly written, buggy, and insecure. Anyone asking for support on Matt’s scripts in any forum will be told in no uncertain terms that they shouldn’t use his scripts.
Unfortunately for some time there were no replacements for Matt’s scripts that you would want people to use. In 2001, the London Perl Mongers decided to address this problem and write a series of drop-in replacements for Matt’s scripts. This project is the result.
That said, you shouldn’t use nms either, because it hasn’t been updated in about 20 years. What gives? After I wrote this,
Dave Cross
, who helped develop the nms tool, reached out and noted that while he still programs in Perl, the mechanisms we use to program and host websites have sharply diverged over the past 30 years. “The best practices in Perl web development moved on from CGI a long time ago,” he wrote in an email.
On top of all that, security practices have continued to evolve.
“The internet is a very different and far less trusting place these days,” Cross added. “One of the problems with FormMail, for example, is that it could be used to send spam. That hole was fixed but, today, things like SPF and DKIM would make it very hard to deliver email to its intended recipient.”
(Even if Cross actually wanted to update the nms scripts, he would be unable to—as he doesn’t have his SourceForge login anymore, nor does he really remember how Subversion works. But we’re not exactly lacking for alternatives, either.)
TFW your old computer is at risk of getting hacked by a guestbook. (
DepositPhotos.com
)
Matt’s scripts, the easy option, and the problem with overexposure
When so many people use something that it becomes part of the internet’s lingua franca, it’s inevitable exploits are going to emerge. There’s a reason WordPress and Windows each have reputations as bug-ridden, and it’s largely because of the number of eyes on the given tools.
With that in mind, I don’t think it’s fair to blame Wright for having bad code—after all, it wasn’t like he knew it was going to become a huge platform.
(For what it’s worth, Wright himself later recommended the nms scripts instead of his own, reminding folks he wrote his original scripts as a kid. “The code you find at Matt’s Script Archive is not representative of how even I would code these days,”
he wrote on his site
. “My interests and activities have moved on, however, and I just have not found the time to update all of my scripts.”)

data.title: Show HN: Wordit – Change One Letter, Keep the Chain Going
data.author: atum47
data.article_summary: 这看起来是一个文字游戏界面，名为 WORDIT。游戏规则是每次改变一个字母来形成新单词，挑战玩家能找到多少个单词。界面包含昵称输入、开始游戏按钮、4字母单词挑战模式，以及排行榜功能（显示顶级玩家）。目前排行榜正在加载中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一个单词变换游戏的用户反馈

不同观点：
• **游戏机制问题**：tty456 指出游戏存在漏洞，找到像"time"这样首字母可替换出多个词的单词后，游戏变得重复无趣，建议增加"困难模式"强制每次更换不同位置的字母
• **与同类游戏对比**：saulpw 提到 Poople 是相同概念但有明确目标且几分钟内可完成，暗示当前游戏缺乏终点设计
• **词典准确性争议**：asimovDev 质疑"ment"作为独立单词被接受（韦氏词典显示它只是后缀）；tim-projects 抱怨"LARP"未被收录
• **改进建议**：vova_hn2 希望游戏结束时展示完整词链并附带词典释义或维基词典链接
• **移动端体验差**：nosioptar 批评手机键盘操作繁琐，每输入一个字母键盘就消失，需要重复点击
• **正面评价**：shwetarkadam257 觉得像 Wordle 很有趣；omeysalvi 和 mgianluc 认为很有娱乐性

补充讨论：
uberex 分享了策略心得（找"buck"这类首字母可大量替换的词）；naikrovek 吐槽起始词"bapt"太难

data.title: Markdy: Like Mermaid Diagrams, but for Motion
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: MarkdyScript 是一个零依赖的纯 TypeScript 动画系统，专为 AI 生成设计。核心特性包括：使用结构化 DSL 语言编写动画脚本，采用 Web Animations API 和 CSS 实现渲染（无 Canvas/GSAP），框架无关可在任何环境使用。提供三个轻量包：核心解析器(~12KB)、DOM 渲染器(~22KB)、Astro 组件(~2KB)。支持场景设置、角色定位、动作序列、时间轴编排等功能，通过简洁的语法创建复杂动画效果，特别适合 LLM 生成和验证动画代码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个表情符号动画工具的展示引发了关于演示内容选择和产品实用性的讨论

不同观点：
• **演示内容不当**：多位评论者批评演示场景（男孩表情为女孩表情争斗）选择不当，认为"cringe"（尴尬）且不专业，这种内容会让技术用户立即离开网站

• **产品潜力肯定**：部分用户认为功能概念有趣，让人联想到Flash时代的创意网络，认为这可能是未来趋势，尤其在年轻用户中有应用前景

• **实用性建议**：建议改用实际应用场景演示，如产品介绍的要点动画、PowerPoint式的文本内容动画，或用于动画化网页组件而非简笔人

• **技术价值质疑**：有用户质疑相比现有工具（如AFrame、AnimeJS）的优势不明确，也有人直接质疑为何能登上首页

• **美学问题**：虽然认可功能，但批评动画的视觉呈现不够吸引人，需要更流畅的动画效果

补充讨论：争议焦点在于产品演示策略——开发者选择了引人注意但不专业的演示内容，反而损害了产品的技术可信度。部分评论还指出内容明显由LLM生成，进一步削弱了专业性。

48646077.article_summary: MarkdyScript 是一个零依赖的纯 TypeScript 动画系统，专为 AI 生成设计。核心特性包括：使用结构化 DSL 语言编写动画脚本，采用 Web Animations API 和 CSS 实现渲染（无 Canvas/GSAP），框架无关可在任何环境使用。提供三个轻量包：核心解析器(~12KB)、DOM 渲染器(~22KB)、Astro 组件(~2KB)。支持场景设置、角色定位、动作序列、时间轴编排等功能，通过简洁的语法创建复杂动画效果，特别适合 LLM 生成和验证动画代码。

主要讨论点：一个表情符号动画工具的展示引发了关于演示内容选择和产品实用性的讨论

不同观点：
• **演示内容不当**：多位评论者批评演示场景（男孩表情为女孩表情争斗）选择不当，认为"cringe"（尴尬）且不专业，这种内容会让技术用户立即离开网站

• **产品潜力肯定**：部分用户认为功能概念有趣，让人联想到Flash时代的创意网络，认为这可能是未来趋势，尤其在年轻用户中有应用前景

• **实用性建议**：建议改用实际应用场景演示，如产品介绍的要点动画、PowerPoint式的文本内容动画，或用于动画化网页组件而非简笔人

• **技术价值质疑**：有用户质疑相比现有工具（如AFrame、AnimeJS）的优势不明确，也有人直接质疑为何能登上首页

• **美学问题**：虽然认可功能，但批评动画的视觉呈现不够吸引人，需要更流畅的动画效果

不同观点：
• **制度设计缺陷论**（zemvpferreira, whizzter）：科研激励机制存在道德风险，应改革学术评价体系，让评审和复现论文成为晋升依据而非发表数量
• **住院医项目责任论**（currymj, spchampion2）：住院医项目不应将招聘决策外包给同行评审系统，应禁止用Medicare培训经费资助研究，医学生做研究缺乏必要训练
• **Step 1改革的连锁反应**（bagelbob432, jmyeet）：Step 1考试改为通过/不通过后，医学生失去了重要的差异化信号，被迫通过堆砌研究项目来增强简历竞争力
• **职业定位困惑**（eunos）：医学界过度强调研究能力，纯粹的临床医生路径不被认可，缺乏研究比临床服务差或缺乏共情更不可接受
• **AI与信息质量担忧**（bigmattystyles）：LLM提供虚假医疗希望很危险，会引用商业网站宣传或曲解医学期刊

补充讨论：
• 有人质疑文章选择性引用极端案例来论证问题（abeppu）

data.title: Show HN: Brain Frog – Can you be random enough for 11 lines of JavaScript?
data.author: AlexanderZ
data.article_summary: 这是一个名为"Brain Frog"的游戏。玩家需要向左或右出拳攻击青蛙，目标是在拳数用完前击中50次。青蛙会根据玩家最近3次出拳的模式来预测并阻挡下一次攻击，因此玩家需要保持不可预测性。游戏提供两种模式：免费练习模式和排位赛模式（花费100金币，获胜可得200金币）。登录后可参与排位赛、查看排行榜并赚取金币。新账户会获得500金币起始奖励。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个互动游戏，玩家需要预测并击打青蛙，涉及随机性、预测算法和游戏机制的讨论

不同观点：
• **情感派**：部分玩家对击打青蛙感到不忍（hash0, digitalWestie），希望给青蛙一个拥抱而非攻击
• **技术分析派**：深入研究游戏机制，尝试用代码作弊（escanor提供了随机和"预测oracle"两种脚本），探讨是否可能做得更好
• **认知偏差观察**：IdiotSavage指出人类的"伪随机"缺乏长序列重复，而真正随机分布经常出现连续相同结果，揭示人们对随机性的误解
• **游戏公平性质疑**：brtkwr认为应该让青蛙也有机会反击才公平
• **创意扩展**：mike_hock建议制作一个对抗各种处理器分支预测器的版本

补充讨论：
- 成绩范围广泛：46-79分不等，显示游戏难度适中
- 排行榜问题：多人发现排行榜被黑客攻击，出现超过100的不可能分数
- 规则理解：有人因误解规则意外进入前十
- 技术细节疑问：询问碰撞检测区域大小、是否使用马尔可夫链等实现细节

data.title: The unbearable cheapness of open weight models
data.author: ddxv
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了AI模型定价的巨大差异。作者在测试Hermes时发现，DeepSeek V4等中国模型的价格比Anthropic和OpenAI的"前沿"模型便宜近50倍。文章质疑OpenAI和Anthropic能否大幅降价竞争，并担心它们可能利用"中国威胁论"推动政府限制开源模型，以制造稀缺性维持高价。作者希望美国能发展真正的开源竞争，特别是Allen AI的OLMo这类数据管道也开源的项目，认为这才是AI的未来方向。文章还提到Google、Meta等公司在开源模型上的表现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源/开放权重AI模型对OpenAI、Anthropic等前沿实验室的商业威胁及行业格局变化

不同观点：

• **乐观派（开源模型将主导）**：推理成本极低且持续下降，95%的AI任务可由开放模型完成，前沿实验室的高价格是品牌溢价而非成本必然，一旦需求下降价格必然跟随。实际使用案例显示通过缓存等技术，月度成本可低至2美元

• **前沿实验室仍有机会派**：巨头可通过两条路径生存——(1)大规模推进前沿能力(网络安全、递归训练、前沿科学)获取溢价；(2)像苹果一样占据应用层，凭借声誉和基础设施优势提供端到端解决方案(医疗、法律、金融等垂直领域)

• **开源未必获胜派**：历史上开源替代品虽优秀但人们仍购买最佳商业产品，AI为何例外？企业需要合同、KPI和问责，受监管行业会偏好闭源方案

• **战略护城河论**：开放权重模型本身就是大公司的护城河策略——通过免费模型提高创业公司的竞争门槛，阻止欧洲等地区开发更好的替代方案

补充讨论：有人质疑DeepSeek等的定价可持续性(称其运营利润率仅70%，GPU折旧成本未充分计入)；也有预测称美国政府可能通过投资和禁令保护本土AI巨头。核心争议在于：信息处理商品化是否会让资本利润率下降，以及企业客户对合同保障的需求能否支撑溢价。

48668255.article_content:
Today I was setting up Hermes to see how it does with web research. I chose DeepSeek V4 because I know it is cheap, but seeing it’s pricing next to Anthropic and OpenAI ‘frontier’ models is crazy. Nearly a 50x price increase based on tokens alone, let alone how much pondering any of their models might fall into (using more tokens for the same task).
What worries me about this is that Anthropic and OpenAI seem to have backed themselves into a corner of high costs. Can they reasonably decrease their prices by 20-50x to compete with DeepSeek or Xiaomi’s Mimo?
Open Weight vs Low Cost
Are these models cheap because they are open weight and having hundreds or people stress test running them on different hardware helped to lower the cost? Or is it that they are being provided as loss leaders to drive the prices down?
How do you keep prices high for commodity products?
You manufacture scarcity. You sell luxury and premium branding. This is what OpenAI and Anthropic seem to be doing by gating ‘frontier’ model usage behind higher walls.
This is how luxury brands have sold cars and hand bags forever. They are clubs and status symbols for the rich and not meant to be widely distributed.
Will Anthropic & OpenAI lean on China fears to push bans on open weight models?
This has been my fear for a few months now and each week that goes by seems to support this. How do you manufacture scarcity? One easy way is to fear monger and get the government to help restrict access to competition.
Why not compete?
The US used to be such a champion of open source, and I would hope that serious open source competition can come out of the US to prove that open weight and open source models are ultimately the future.
Google Gemma 4 was released in April 2026
Meta had llama which hasn’t had a release
OpenAI last released open weight gpt models in 2025
Anthropic to my knowledge has never released any open weight model
True Open Source vs Open Weight
I think the leap frog scenario for Open Source will be the true Open Source models where the data pipeline for training is also open sourced.
https://allenai.org/olmo
-> You can download these models now and they’re seeing increasing popularity. That being said, they are a bit out of date, with data cutoffs in Dec 2024
Looking to the future, the US NSF partnered with Nvidia to enable Allen AI to develop a true fully open AI:
https://www.nsf.gov/news/nsf-nvidia-partnership-enables-ai2-develop-fully-open-ai

data.title: Writers and Drugs
data.author: dang
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了艺术家和作家与药物滥用的历史关联。作者列举了大量文学史上的药物使用案例：伏尔泰和巴尔扎克狂饮咖啡，拜伦、济慈、柯勒律治沉迷鸦片，弗洛伊德和史蒂文森使用可卡因，波德莱尔等人吸食大麻。文章指出这些化学物质最终会先摧毁作品，再毁掉艺术家本人。作者还提到了一些历史细节，如可卡因曾被视为"奇迹物质"，以及麦角菌可能影响了圣女特蕾莎等神秘主义者的幻觉体验。整体上，文章呈现了创作者们试图通过药物来解放情感、消除自我控制、寻找灵感的悲剧性历史。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：艺术家酗酒现象的成因及影响

不同观点：
• **敏感性假说**（garethsprice）：艺术家天生高度敏感，既被创作吸引也需要酒精麻痹过度刺激。随着饮酒变得不被社会接受和心理健康知识普及，未来可能出现更少酗酒的公众人物，但艺术质量会否因此改变仍是疑问。

• **药物可获得性因素**（zabzonk）：酒精流行是因为合法易得且具社交性，不像海洛因那样受限。举例William S. Burroughs长寿暗示海洛因可能伤害更小。

• **衰老代谢论**（sublinear）：问题不在于饮酒量，而是衰老的代谢现实。多数人三四十岁会减少饮酒，但这些作家因生活方式不够灵活、担心失去机会和死亡恐惧而继续酗酒。

• **自我意识缺失的悲剧**（vintagedave）：最可怕的是作家们明知酒精毁灭生活，却不知道成瘾后作品质量持续下降甚至完全沉默，缺乏自我认知导致宝贵创造力的丧失。

• **才华与痛苦的关联**（none2585）：才华横溢的人往往备受折磨，因此转向自我药疗寻求逃避。

补充讨论：有人提出大麻未被提及（可能更受音乐家青睐），以及在鼓励表达自由的社群中，若无药物"解放"会有多少杰作诞生的疑问。

Are Writers Intrinsically Vulnerable to Alcohol and Drugs?
Rosa Montero on the Impact of Substance Abuse on Generations of Writers
Via Europa Editions
Rosa Montero
June 4, 2026
The history of art in general, and literature in particular, is full of alcoholics, opium addicts, cocaine users, and junkies of all sorts. And the process is always the same: the chemical muse kills first the work, and then the artist. “Then I was drunk for many years, and then I died,” F. Scott Fitzgerald wrote in a diary.
Article continues after advertisement
Interestingly, one drug that had its moment among creators was coffee: Voltaire drank fifty coffees a day, Balzac forty, and Flaubert paired his dozens of daily cups with glasses of ice water. Nietzsche was addicted to chloral hydrate, a sedative made from chloroform; Freud and Robert Louis Stevenson, to cocaine; Ramón del Valle-Inclán smoked hashish heavily—just as Baudelaire had done in 1840, as a member of the Club des Hashischins, together with writers such as Honoré de Balzac, Théophile Gautier, Gérard de Nerval, and the painter Eugène Delacroix. Opium in particular has always had a strong following. “Of all drugs, opium is the drug,” said Jean Cocteau. “It gives form to the formless.” And isn’t that what all artists are seeking?
Opium was used by Shelley, Wordsworth, Byron, Keats, Flaubert, Rimbaud. Thomas De Quincey enthused that opium drew back the veil “between our present consciousness and the secret inscriptions on the mind.” Incidentally, the badly addicted De Quincey ended up suffering terribly, experiencing severe dissociation and horrific nightmares. Not to mention perhaps the most famous opium addict in the history of literature, Samuel Taylor Coleridge, whose renowned poem “Kubla Khan” came to him in a drug-induced dream (he woke up and hurriedly jotted down the lines, but could only remember part of it). Even someone like Octavio Paz, a formidable writer who gave the impression of being a very formal and serious gentleman, once said: “Drugs […] give life to analogy, put objects in motion, make of the world a vast poem of rhythms and rhymes.”
I understand what led them to alcohol. It’s as we said at the beginning: to heighten the emotions, enhance disinhibition, quell the controlling self.
As for cocaine, once it was first extracted from coca plants in 1860 it was immediately hailed as a miracle substance: the market was flooded with coca pills, syrups, and elixirs. Jules Verne thought it “a wonderful tonic.” The young and enterprising Mark Twain contemplated setting up a business that consisted of going to the Amazon to harvest coca in order to “open up a trade in coca with all the world.” For months he pondered the project, even setting off for Peru with a 50 dollar bill in his pocket that he’d found on the street, but he only made it as far as New Orleans. This incredible story is recounted by Sadie Plant in her fascinating book
Writing on Drugs
. She also reveals that, according to some authors, the visions of St. Teresa of Jesus and other mystics may have been facilitated by psychoactive substances, such as ergot. Ergot is a fungus that attacks cereal crops; consuming the infected flour of these crops can lead to a disease called St. Anthony’s Fire, which was quite common in the Middle Ages and causes terrible symptoms: seizures, dementia, and fatal gangrenous infections. However, if taken in small quantities, it can induce hallucinations. Ergot contains an alkaloid, ergoline, from which LSD was synthesized in 1938.
Before that, ergotamine had also been extracted from it, a medication for migraines that I have taken in large doses throughout my life (this has nothing to do with the story: I was just stunned to discover it). I’d previously read about the probable influence of ergot on painters such as Bosch (those kaleidoscopic deliriums), but I was unaware of the mystics. And Sadie Plant goes on to recount something even more shocking: scientist John Mann apparently discovered a connection between certain historical events and periods when the climate was favorable to the growth of ergot, which may have provoked a kind of collective hallucination. data.author: exploraz
data.article_summary:
这是Dolphin模拟器2606版本的进度报告。主要更新包括：

1. **Game Boy Player支持**：通过集成mGBA模拟器，实现了对GameCube的Game Boy Player外设的模拟，可在Dolphin中运行GB/GBC/GBA游戏。

2. **Triforce游戏支持**：最后一款无法运行的Triforce街机游戏《The Key of Avalon》现已可玩，支持最多5个模拟器实例联机。

3. **RetroAchievements扩展**：成就系统现已支持Wii游戏。

4. **图形优化**：修复了高分辨率下困扰旗舰游戏多年的重大视觉问题。

文章详细介绍了Game Boy Player模拟的技术挑战及实现过程。

Welcome to the Progress Report for Dolphin Release 2606.  We usually prefer to launch toward the beginning of the month, but a slew of important, large, and technically challenging changes had us working overtime.  Strap in, because we have a lot to cover!
For April Fool's we teased that Dolphin now had support for the Game Boy Player, but the joke was that
it was real!
We'll detail exactly how it happened and the challenges that surrounded getting the emulated hardware and software working together. The last unplayable Triforce game,
The Key of Avalon
, no longer has that title!  It is now functional in Dolphin, supporting up to
five
instances of the emulator together for 4 player (and a server) action. And Graphics Mods quietly fixed a major visual issue at high resolution that has plagued many flagship games for Dolphin's entire existence!
All of that and more in this Dolphin Progress Re-
✱ knock knock knock ✱
Huh, someone's at the door. Could you get that?
That's right! Since the last Dolphin Progress Report, RetroAchievements support has come to Wii games. You can now waggle your way up the leaderboard! We'll go over some statistics of the launch in a section down below, which you can reach with
this handy link
!
Without further ado, let's get to the Notable Changes for Dolphin 2606!
Notable Changes
¶
All changes below are available in Release 2606.
2603-175 - HW:  Game Boy Player Support
by
Billiard
and
endrift
¶
The
Game Boy
family of
handhelds
are legends of a bygone era. Under the crushing weight of incredibly primitive technology, Nintendo chose to focus on portability and great games rather than pushing the latest and greatest hardware.
They were right.
The Game Boy line outsold every single competitor they ever faced!
However, as great games accumulated on the platform, demand began to build for a way to play them on nicer, larger,
lit
screens. Nintendo eventually answered it with the
Super Game Boy
for the
Super Famicom/Super Nintendo
, and its
Advance
'd successor, the
Game Boy Player
for the Nintendo GameCube.
These devices were
literally
Game Boys without a screen that plugged into a home console, transmitting audio and video to the host console and receiving input from its controller. Software running on the host console would handle
interfacing
between the two systems and sometimes could add additional features if a game supported it.
We imagine that Nintendo chose to use actual Game Boy hardware because of the difficulty of making a general-purpose software emulator.  The perfect demonstration of this is a third-party competitor to the Game Boy Player, the
Advance Game Port
, which attempted just that!  By creating a Game Boy Advance emulator, Datel was able to ship a lower cost way to play GBA games on a GameCube. It was very ahead of its time, but also
very flawed
.
This is a 60 FPS GBA game running the Advance Game Port emulator within Dolphin. The flat blue line (V-Blank) at 16.6ms shows the game is running at "full speed". But the orange line (actual frametime) should be exactly the same as the blue line. It's not. In order to run their Game Boy Advance emulator at "full speed" on a GameCube, Datel frameskips 2 out of every 3 frames, for a
maximum
of
20 FPS
.
Nintendo showed that they could do emulation better on a
per-game
basis with titles like
Pokémon Box
, but they didn't see it as a plausible solution for the entire library. By shipping actual GBA hardware, the Game Boy Player was able to bypass all performance and compatibility concerns.
Being a peripheral for the GameCube, emulating the Game Boy Player has always been in the back of our minds. There was even an feature request for it for
over 16 years
!  But it languished on the issue tracker and became the oldest open issue for one simple reason: emulating the Game Boy Player would essentially mean emulating a Game Boy Advance (which potentially involves making a new GBA emulator from scratch)
and
how it communicates to the GameCube.  There was no way anyone would be willing to volunteer the gargantuan effort necessary just for an amusing curiosity.
Ultimately, the feature request was accepted, but there was really no path forward for it back then.  We just recommended that users use one of the many available GB/GBC/GBA emulators already available, and figured that would be the end of it.  They could even use the Advance Game Port in Dolphin if they really needed to run GBA games in Dolphin, as that peripheral has been partially supported
since the 4.0 era
.
For the longest time, the feature request was completely dormant, until around five years ago.  Support for the Game Boy Player became a bit more realistic when
mGBA was integrated into Dolphin
. It was the ultimate solution to emulating the Game Boy Advance connectivity features found in some GameCube games, fixing all of the synchronization and communication issues that had plagued the feature for years in one fell swoop. With this, the tables had turned on Game Boy Pla

补充讨论：多位评论者担心AI虽提高效率和准确性,但会削弱写作的个性、深度和人际连接功能

data.title: Bohemia Interactive: Cold War Assault Remastered Source Code on GitHub
data.author: dewey
data.article_summary: 这是Bohemia Interactive公司开源的《武装突袭：冷战突击》(原名《闪点行动》)游戏引擎和源代码仓库。代码已现代化为C++20，支持Windows和Linux平台，采用GPL-3.0-or-later许可证发布。需要注意三点：1)源代码开源可自由修改；2)"ARMA"等商标不授权使用，分支项目必须改名；3)游戏数据(模型、贴图等)不包含在此仓库中，需单独从Steam获取Demo版本，受APL-SA协议约束。代码面向保持游戏20多年活力的社区开放，供学习、构建和改进使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Bohemia Interactive开源Operation Flashpoint/Cold War Assault游戏引擎代码

不同观点：
• **技术成就派**：认为Poseidon引擎在2001年就实现了12.5km×12.5km大地图、模组化设计和运行时脚本语言，领先Half-Life 2三年，技术远超时代
• **游戏体验派**：虽然ARMA系列"janky"（不稳定），但比现代战争/战地系列更沉浸，强调团队沟通的重要性；Operation Flashpoint是系列最佳作品
• **开源贡献派**：赞赏BI不仅开源还清理代码并移植到x64和Linux，希望更多厂商效仿（如育碧的细胞分裂系列）；GPL3.0协议让社区可以学习和改造资源
• **历史情怀派**：回忆游戏独特的"纸质/干燥"视觉风格，当年在爱沙尼亚很流行；有开发者因为编写任务简报学HTML而走上职业开发道路

补充讨论：
- 代码质量比DayZ基础的VBS2版本更好，DayZ的bug源于引擎未预期的长期使用
- 游戏有趣的反作弊机制：盗版可以玩但准星会逐渐变差
- 这是"Stop Killing Games"运动的理想案例，既是可玩demo又是官方资源包

Arma: Cold War Assault - Remastered
This repository holds the engine and game source code (codename
Poseidon
) behind
Arma: Cold War Assault
— the game first released in 2001 as
Operation Flashpoint: Cold War Crisis
. That release launched Bohemia Interactive and began the technology lineage that later grew into Real Virtuality, Arma, and Enfusion. The code has been modernized to C++20, built with CMake and Clang, with cross-platform support for Windows x64 and Linux x64.
Bohemia Interactive is releasing it to the community that has kept this game alive for more than two decades — to study it, build on it, fix it, and create from it. Three things are worth keeping separate:
Source code (this repository)

48636753.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Bohemia Interactive开源Operation Flashpoint/Cold War Assault游戏引擎代码

不同观点：
• **技术成就派**：认为Poseidon引擎在2001年就实现了12.5km×12.5km大地图、模组化设计和运行时脚本语言，领先Half-Life 2三年，技术远超时代
• **游戏体验派**：虽然ARMA系列"janky"（不稳定），但比现代战争/战地系列更沉浸，强调团队沟通的重要性；Operation Flashpoint是系列最佳作品

data.title: Wikipedia Workers in Britain set global first by seeking union recognition
data.author: chobeat
data.article_summary: 英国维基媒体基金会(WMF)的员工成为全球首个寻求工会认可的维基百科工作者群体。他们于6月24日致信管理层,要求由通信工会(CWU)下属的联合科技工人组织(UTAW)代表其权益。近几个月WMF经历重大变革,员工对透明度、信任和组织方向感到担忧。超过1000名维基百科志愿者和社区成员签署请愿书支持这些工作者。英国是WMF在美国之外最大的雇佣地,大多数英国员工已加入工会。工会呼吁组织以诚信和合作精神回应员工诉求。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：维基媒体基金会英国员工组建工会的消息引发的讨论

不同观点：
• **支持工会方**：认为组建工会是员工的权利和最佳利益所在，管理层应当接受这一合理诉求（Frieren、ggm等）
• **怀疑工会效用方**：认为工会在欧洲实际上保护效果有限，主要增加解雇成本、降低流动性，还会产生内部利益输送问题（christkv）；甚至有人极端地认为工会只收会费并资助共产主义者（crunchiepooker）
• **欧盟税收优惠视角**：指出在欧盟成立工会有实际税务好处，如会费免税、可组织免税活动等（throw93949444）
• **概念澄清方**：强调新闻稿混淆了"维基百科编辑者"和"维基媒体基金会员工"这两个不同概念，这是工会方面的错误（JdeBP）
• **担忧工会后果方**：担心工会成立后，超过半数不积极的员工也会受保护而无法被解雇（philipallstar）

补充讨论：有人指出这是重复讨论的话题，并询问DeepMind工会进展；有评论讽刺维基百科编辑者的派系问题。整体讨论呈现出对工会制度的分歧态度。

48669932.article_content:
Wikipedia workers in Britain are setting a global first by becoming the first body of workers at the online encyclopaedia to seek union recognition.
British-based employees at the Wikimedia Foundation (WMF) wrote a letter to management today, Wednesday 24th of June requesting their right to be represented by the United Tech and Allied Workers (UTAW) section of the Communication Workers Union (CWU)
The workers have called on the WMF, as the effective management of the global non-profit operation, to uphold recent public commitments made by its leadership affirming the rights of staff to organise and form a union.
The WMF has undergone a period of significant change in recent months, escalating workers’ concerns over transparency, trust, and the organisation’s future direction.
The workers are longtime contributors and organisers, and are deeply committed to the Wikimedia movement.
Over 1000 Wikimedia volunteers and community members have also signed petitions in support of the workers, who have networked globally under the banner of Wiki Workers United (WWU).
The WMF is the non-profit organisation that operates Wikipedia and its sister projects. Collectively, they represent the world’s largest free knowledge websites, written and maintained by a global set of volunteers.
Outside of the United States, the United Kingdom is WMF’s largest employment location, and a substantial majority of its UK staff are union members.
“
Our union is proud to stand with these principled workers, who are initiating this process in the hope of creating a durable workplace grounded in transparency, accountability and participation across the WMF workforce.
We urge the organisation to meet them in this spirit of good faith and co-operation.
”

John Chadfield, CWU National Officer for Tech

data.title: Lies, Damn Lies and Database Benchmarks
data.author: eigenBasis
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论数据库基准测试的公平性问题，以ClickBench为例。ClickBench对100多个数据库系统运行相同的分析查询工作负载，测量冷运行和热运行性能。文章指出基准测试存在隐藏的不对称性：自托管数据库需要清除缓存和重启服务器进行真正的冷运行测试，而云托管服务无法做到这点，导致结果偏向云服务。作者聚焦于热运行结果，并解释ClickBench的评分机制是基于各数据库相对于最快系统的几何平均比率。文章强调完全公平的数据库基准测试像独角兽一样难以实现，不同类型数据库的比较尤其复杂。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数据库性能基准测试的诚信问题，以及QuestDB在生产环境中的使用情况

不同观点：
• **基准测试作弊普遍存在**：多位评论者指出这是行业常态，从90年代Oracle/Sybase/IBM的TPC-C基准战，到近期Terminal Bench和Spacetime DB的争议，厂商会针对基准测试优化而非真实场景
• **ClickBench本身存在局限**：有人认为ClickBench缺乏JOIN测试，实用性有限，可能因为ClickHouse本身不擅长JOIN操作
• **冷启动测试的合理性争议**：有评论认为反对测量冷启动查询的观点不完整——如果系统五年重启一次，20分钟预热可接受；但若每小时重启则是严重问题，需要结合实际使用场景判断
• **QuestDB使用咨询**：原帖询问生产环境经验，想从InfluxDB迁移（因其开源政策反复和频繁重构产品）

补充讨论：评论者普遍认为这类问题不仅存在于数据库领域，LLM基准测试也面临同样挑战。有人赞赏QuestDB团队的透明度和写作质量。整体讨论反映出技术社区对基准测试可信度的担忧和对诚实行为的重视。

48639429.article_content:
QuestDB is the open-source time-series database for demanding workloads—from trading floors to mission control.
It delivers ultra-low latency, high ingestion throughput, and a multi-tier storage engine.
Native support for Parquet and SQL keeps your data portable, AI-ready—no vendor lock-in.
Benchmarks, everyone loves benchmarks. People look at a benchmark result and
start spreading the word that database X is the top dog, since it is so much
faster than database Y.
A decent benchmark might be pictured as a strict Olympic
Games-like running competition where the "Citius, Altius, Fortius" principle is
precisely implemented. But in reality, when you approach the athletes, you start
hearing unexpected noises. What is that? It turns out the competition is more
like those weird contests you find on the Internet: the athletes must whistle
"Yellow Submarine" accurately while running as fast as they can. The winner is no
longer the fastest runner. It is whoever best balances raw speed against a skill
that has nothing to do with running, and the quickest sprinter on the track can
easily finish last.
That analogy applies to a thing as complex as database benchmarks, especially
when quite different categories of databases are being compared. A perfect,
completely fair database benchmark is like a unicorn: good luck finding one.
Today we will try to illustrate this by toying with a public, well-recognized
benchmark.
The benchmark we will use is
ClickBench
, but do not get us
wrong: we are here to question all database benchmarks, not ClickBench
specifically. ClickBench is just convenient. It is a solid comparison for
analytical databases and already includes a large roster of engines.
How ClickBench measures things
ClickBench runs the same workload against every system: a single web-analytics
table of around 100 million rows and 105 columns (the famous
hits
dataset),
and 43 analytical queries over it. Each engine ships a small set of shell
scripts. The flow is always the same: a script installs the database, loads the
data (importing from CSV/TSV, or simply pointing the engine at a downloaded
Parquet file if it can read external files), and then runs the 43 queries.
Each query is measured in two flavors:
Cold run.
This is the first execution of a query, with all operating
system page caches and database caches cleared beforehand. It captures the
worst case, when nothing is warm.
Hot run.
Quoting the ClickBench rules, "each of the 43 queries is run
three times," and "the smaller of the 2nd and 3rd runtime is used if both runs
are successful." The first run is supposed to populate the caches, so the two
later runs are expected to be the fastest.
That cold definition hides an asymmetry the public dashboard does not advertise.
Clearing the OS page cache and restarting the server is only possible when the
database runs on the benchmark machine. A managed cloud service, say Snowflake,
BigQuery, Redshift, or Databricks, runs on the provider's hardware, where the
harness has no shell, no
drop_caches
, and no way to bounce the server, so its
three runs all hit the same live, never-restarted service. Its cold number is
therefore never forced cold the way a self-hosted engine's is, which tilts the
cold-run ranking toward hosted systems, and with it the combined score that folds
cold runs in. ClickBench's rules require that restart for a true cold run, and a
restart is something you can only ask of a server you control. Every engine in
this post runs self-hosted on the same box, so they all play by the same rule,
but it is worth remembering the next time you compare cold-run numbers across
hosted and self-managed systems.
We will focus on hot-run results only. We will not compare individual queries
either, only the overall score. The score is the one the public dashboard
shows: for each query, ClickBench computes a ratio against the fastest system on
that query,
ratio = (0.01 + hot_time) / (0.01 + baseline_time)
where
baseline_time
is the best hot time among the compared systems for that
query. The
0.01
is a 10 ms cushion that stops sub-10 ms queries from
dominating. The final score is the
geometric mean
of those ratios
across all 43 queries. Lower is better, and a hypothetical
1.000
would mean "fastest on
every single query." A failed query is penalized heavily. The full results for
everything below live in the support repository linked at the end, so you can
re-score them yourself.
INFO
Here is the subtlety that drives this entire post. Every ClickBench
query
script records the engine's own
internal
query time: DuckDB's
Run Time
,
ClickHouse's
--time
, DataFusion's
Elapsed
, QuestDB's
timings.execute
, Polars' internal
elapsed
. Process and client startup is in nobody's recorded
number. So keeping a process alive cannot change the score by removing a startup
term, because that term was never in the number to begin with. It can only
change the score through process-local cache warmth. Keep this in mind, it
matters later.
The test

data.title: LastPass notifies users of yet another data breach
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: LastPass通知用户其合作伙伴Klue遭遇数据泄露。黑客获取了客户联系信息、CRM数据、支持案例和销售数据，包括姓名、电话、邮箱和地址。LastPass强调密码保险库未受影响，并已撤销员工访问权限、轮换API令牌并通知执法部门。公司建议用户警惕钓鱼攻击。这是LastPass继2015年和2022年安全事件后的又一次数据泄露。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LastPass通过合作伙伴Klue遭遇数据泄露事件，引发用户对其安全性的质疑和密码管理方案的讨论。

不同观点：
• **彻底不信任派**：认为LastPass在历史安全事件后已失去信任，应立即迁移。有用户提到2022年vault泄露事件后仍选择LastPass的公司"不在乎安全"。甚至有人建议先导出到Google Sheets也比继续用LastPass安全。

• **理性看待派**：指出此次泄露仅涉及CRM数据（姓名、邮箱、地址等商业联系信息），并非密码库本身，影响有限。认为不必过度恐慌。

• **迁移成本考量派**：承认从LastPass迁移到其他服务（如1Password）是"大工程且极其烦人"，理解企业用户继续使用的困境，但仍不赞同2022年后新选择LastPass的行为。

• **替代方案推荐**：
  - BitWarden、KeepassXC（本地数据库+自选同步）
  - Enpass（使用用户自己的云存储同步，避免集中式数据库风险）
  - Apple Passwords、Google Chrome密码管理器（依赖大厂安全投入）

补充讨论：争议焦点在于LastPass为何将客户数据交给市场研究公司Klue且未充分匿名化。部分用户采用"忘记90%密码，需要时重置"的极简策略。

48671468.article_content:
LastPass
LastPass notifies users of yet another data breach
Marcus Mendes
| Jun 23 2026 - 2:48 pm PT
3 Comments
LastPass users are once again being warned about stolen personal data, though this time the breach happened through one of the company’s outside partners. Here are the details.
LastPass says password vaults not affected
As reported by
TechCrunch
, LastPass is emailing users affected by a
breach at market research firm Klue
, which allowed hackers to access customer information and support case data.
The news came as LastPass shared more information on a
blog post
, where it explained:
The information accessed was limited to standard business contact information and related customer relationship management (CRM) data, including customer names, phone numbers, email addresses, and physical addresses, as well as support case data and sales-related data.
LastPass said that upon learning about the incident, the company revoked employee access to Klue, rotated the exposed API tokens, notified law enforcement, and launched “a detailed investigation into the scope of the event, working with our contacts at both Klue and Salesforce.”
The company explains that Klue’s platform integrates with Salesforce and Gong systems.
As a result, LastPass is recommending that customers “remain vigilant of potential phishing attacks or social engineering attempts” leveraging the compromised information. LastPass also shared the following IP addresses and email sender domains associated with the attackers, which companies can use to search for related activity in their systems:
IP Addresses:
138.226.246[.]94
94.154.32[.]160
159.183.215[.]61
159.183.181[.]239
Email Sender Domains:
baccarat.com[.]au
robinskitchen.com[.]au
house.com[.]au
This is the latest in a series of security incidents affecting LastPass. In
2015
, hackers obtained account email addresses, password reminders, authentication hashes, and cryptographic salts, although LastPass said encrypted vault data was not accessed.
In
2022
, an attacker compromised a developer account and stole source code and technical information. The attacker later used that information to access cloud backups containing customer records and encrypted password vaults, along with unencrypted details such as names, billing addresses, email addresses, and phone numbers⁠.

data.title: Puzzling Success of Overparameterization: Lottery Tickets or Escape Dimensions?
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary:
这篇论文质疑了用"彩票假说"解释过参数化神经网络成功的流行观点。作者认为，将学习过程比作"买更多彩票增加中奖概率"的类比是误导性的，因为它忽略了子网络与整体网络的相互依赖关系。

论文提出了基于损失函数几何形状的新解释：增加网络宽度扩展了优化的可用维度，使网络更容易逃离局部最优解。随着宽度增长，劣质局部最优相对于良好最优变得越来越稀少。作者强调需要用更准确的类比来解释大型网络的冗余现象，以协调实践直觉与现代理论洞察。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：神经网络过参数化为何能够泛化而非过拟合

不同观点：
• **Hessian特征值视角**（cherryteastain）：过参数化有利于优化，因为参数越多，Hessian矩阵所有特征值同时为正/零的概率呈指数级下降，模型更不易陷入局部最优

• **决策边界合并机制**（HarHarVeryFunny）：过参数化网络在结构化数据上的泛化源于训练动态过程——初期学习"零散"的决策边界（过拟合），随后若数据标签一致，这些边界会逐渐合并成更大区域，实现泛化。关键在于数据流形的一致性标注使得合并成为可能

• **参数空间搜索视角**（Scene_Cast2）：过参数化相当于在参数空间中"任意位置生成高斯函数"，避免了简单模型因初始位置不佳而梯度消失的问题，代价是参数冗余

补充讨论：
vatsachak指出过参数化能泛化并非新发现，真正有趣的是"双下降"现象的机制。Scene_Cast2提到彩票假说（Lottery Ticket Hypothesis）的原作者已否认该理论，暗示对过参数化的理解仍在演进中。

48657481.article_content:
preprint
The Puzzling Success of Overparameterization: Lottery Tickets or Escape Dimensions?
Martinelli, Flavio
•
Brea, Johanni
•
Gerstner, Wulfram
May 12, 2026
Lotteries and tickets are often used as a didactical analogy to explain the success of overparameterized neural networks: “larger networks succeed because they more likely contain a well-initialized subnetwork that can learn the task in isolation, much like buying more tickets increases the chances of winning a lottery.”
This explanation is intuitive but misleading: it suggests that subnetworks can be treated in isolation from the rest of the network. Following this reasoning leads to interpreting learning in wide networks as a multi-start optimization process, where gradient descent simply conducts a parallel search over subnetworks. We argue that this view is flawed since, among other reasons, winning tickets can be made to fail by perturbing the rest of the network.
We put forward a more accurate intuitive picture for the success of overparameterization based on the geometry of loss landscapes: increasing width expands the set of available dimensions for optimization, making it easier to escape bad local minima. Moreover, as width grows, bad minima become increasingly rare relative to good minima.
As the field grows mature, it is important to refine the analogies we use to explain foundational phenomena, such as the apparent redundancy of large networks, reconciling practitioners' intuitions with modern theoretical insights.

data.title: Countries are competing to see which can carry out mass surveillance the best
data.author: Cider9986
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论大规模监控问题，分为商业监控和国家监控两类。文章认为大规模监控侵犯人权和隐私，应只对犯罪嫌疑人进行针对性监控。重点揭露美国的全球监控能力：通过《外国情报监视法》第702条，NSA可监控全球数亿人。斯诺登2013年曝光NSA每天收集2亿条短信、监控互联网活动，使用Xkeyscore程序访问邮件、聊天记录等私人数据。文章强调人权保护的重要性，批评政府滥用权力进行无差别监控。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：互联网正在从开放走向集中化监控，多国政府和企业正在加强数字监控体系

不同观点：
• **悲观派**：认为互联网自由已成"瓶中闪电"，不可逆转地走向中心化和实名制。商业VPN只是延缓而非解决方案，最终也会被要求实名或禁止（0x_rs, egorfine）
• **现实案例派**：指出新加坡、中国、英国等国已建立成熟监控体系，新加坡甚至实现民众互相监督。Reddit开始要求KYC验证，HN可能两年内跟进（GL26, egorfine, sys_64738）
• **动机分析派**：认为监控主要针对外国影响和间谍活动的冷战，而非犯罪。提到加拿大面临的中国选举干预和印度间谍事件（speak_plainly）
• **技术中立派**：指出VPN确实被大量用于攻击和滥用，封锁有其合理性（goalieca）
• **商业模式批判派**：认为科技公司的"免费软件换监控"模式本质上是用软件作诱饵进行监控牟利，与传统银行仅监控商业交易不同（1vuio0pswjnm7）
• **替代方案派**：提出非西方国家可能发展独立的互联网治理模式，如尼日利亚的.ng域名（TestINGNG）

补充讨论：有评论指出根本解决方案是自制芯片以避免被控制（MomsAVoxell），也有人质疑为何各国突然同时推进监控（ranger_danger）

There are two types of mass surveillance.
Commercial, which you can read about here
. And mass surveillance carried out by states and rulers. Both are reprehensible, and our attitude is well-established: mass surveillance infringes individualsâ
human rights
, invades the personal privacy free societies are built on, and is also ineffective against the problems itâs claimed to solve. This is the ultimate core of our business. Our company was founded in 2009 because the surveillance laws were going in the wrong direction, and our message to those in power all over the world is the same now as it was then: thereâs a difference between surveillance and mass surveillance. Donât get involved with the latter: donât carry out mass surveillance on your population or that of other countries. Use targeted surveillance if thereâs a suspicion of a crime, in a proportional way and via independent court decisions.
We think human rights are worth preserving and defending. And itâs important to remember that theyâre there to protect people against the state. They are a landmark to cling to, to prevent the worst parts of human history repeating themselves. They are there because people and those in power take bad decisions. Because governments change. Because no state should have total and uncontrollable power. Ultimately, the state should be there for the people and not the other way round
Even if a large part of todayâs mass surveillance is global, it originates in different countries and changes depending on what country you live in.
You can read about the consequences of mass surveillance here
. But in this article, weâre going to take a look at some of the clearest examples of how widespread it has become in large parts of the world.
USA: with the capacity and experience of monitoring the entire population of the world.
Thereâs a problem with reporting the mass surveillance carried out by countries like the USA (at least if you want to stick to proven facts): they arenât very happy about you talking about it. Of course there are exceptions. Like when self-satisfied managers like the CIAâs chief technology officer Ira âGusâ Hunt give presentations and boast to journalists about how
âwe try to collect everything and hang onto it foreverâ
. Or when a senior Defense Department official explains that not even the Pentagonâs employees can expect to have their privacy respected: âWe want our people to understand: they should make no assumptions about anonymity. You are not anonymous on this planet at this point in our existence. Everyone is trackable, traceable, discoverable to some degreeâ.
And sometimes a building says more than a thousand words, like when
the NSA constructs enormous server halls out in the Utah desert to store data
.
But to get mass surveillance down in black-and-white, to produce hard facts and figures, it requires brave whistleblowers like Edward Snowden. Itâs only through this type of hero that we get an insight into whatâs actually going on. Even now we still donât have better answers than what Snowden gave us in 2013. Weâd hoped for change in the wake of his revelations, but unfortunately theyâre still relevant today, so thatâs where weâll start.
Snowden's revelations showed that American authorities were monitoring hundreds of millions of people all over the world â every day.
American mass surveillance is possible thanks to
Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA)
, a law that the USA renews every five years. Section 702 is the key to why American authorities need no court decisions to monitor people. The law came into being on the pretext that terrorists were being tracked after the 9/11 attacks, and would âonlyâ refer to eavesdropping on non-American citizens, but as the law is written and as the internet is constructed, in practice it means surveillance of both foreign and American citizens. When Snowdenâs revelations emerged, it also turned out that it wasnât just being used against people suspected of a crime, but that the American administration was carrying out
mass surveillance of millions of people
. Other documents that Snowden leaked demonstrated how the National Security Agency (NSA) had the capacity to monitor essentially every person on the planet, and that they werenât saving their powder: the documents showed, amongst other things that they collected
200 million text messages
from different parts of the world â every day.
Using the program Xkeyscore, the NSAâs analysts had access to a database covering
ânearly everything a typical user does on the internetâ
. This included both direct data like emails in peopleâs inboxes, chat conversations and private messages on Facebook. But also things categorized as metadata; search histories and exactly what sites millions of people were visiting.

• **替代方案派**：提出非西方国家可能发展独立的互联网治理模式，如尼日利亚的.ng域名（TestINGNG）

补充讨论：有评论指出根本解决方案是自制芯片以避免被控制（MomsAVoxell），也有人质疑为何各国突然同时推进监控（ranger_danger）

AAPL Company
Apple announces significant price increases for MacBooks, iPads, more
Chance Miller
| Jun 25 2026 - 5:43 am PT
10 Comments
Apple has raised prices across the board for many of its products today. MacBook Neo now starts at $699 (up from $599), while MacBook Air now starts at $1299 (up from $1099). Other impacted products include MacBook Pro, iPad, iPad Air, and many more.
iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods pricing is unchanged.
Why is Apple increasing prices?
Apple CEO Tim Cook
confirmed the company
would increase product prices in an interview last week. Cook explained that price increases had simply become “unavoidable” amid skyrocketing component costs affecting things like memory and storage. While Apple tried to weather the storm itself, the situation was ultimately “unsustainable.”
“We’re doing our best to mitigate the huge increases that are being passed to us, and we’ve been trying to shield our customers from the increases, but the situation has become unsustainable,” Cook said in the interview.
Cook specifically called out the increasing amount of memory going to high-bandwidth memory used for AI servers. “There’s less supply at a time when consumers want devices and the memory guys are passing along huge price increases,” he said.
In a statement to
Reuters
today, Apple said:
“We have never ​seen a component price increase this much, this quickly. We have shielded our customers ⁠from these increases so far, but we have now reached a point where we need to begin raising prices on a number of products, including ​today’s increases for iPad and Mac. We know this is not welcome news, and we are working tirelessly to find solutions.”

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：日本动画行业人才流失与产业困境

不同观点：

• **行业结构问题论**（frmersdog, jdw64）：问题核心在于只重视顶尖人才而忽视"足够好"的基层动画师。日本动画师月薪仅1300美元，年工作2745小时（周均52小时），平台资本主义导致价值集中于少数IP和明星创作者，基层劳动者被排除在外。这是全球发达国家就业市场的共同问题。

• **技术进步与成本优化论**（hibikir）：外包、3D技术和AI是市场竞争的必然结果。现代动画质量和产量都超过90年代，技术优化让更多作品得以制作。如果坚持传统手绘，高成本会导致产量锐减，只有大热作品能获得资金。

• **工艺价值坚守论**（hiccuphippo, heldrida）：《葬送的芙莉莲》第二季片尾全手绘、新版《攻壳机动队》坚持手绘证明传统工艺仍有价值。AI生成内容质量低劣，真正的工艺无法被替代。

• **内容质量下滑论**（world2vec）：尽管动画更流行，但质量下降，充斥异世界和卖肉题材，值得看的作品越来越少。

补充讨论：
有人提出AI应辅助而非替代动画师（rendaw），让AI处理上色和中间帧；多人指出这是跨行业现象，教师、护士、游戏开发者都因"热情"被压榨工资（hyfgfh, jmclnx）。

data.title: You can't unit test for taste
data.author: kalli
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讲述了作者为跑步应用"In the Long Run"开发景点推荐功能的过程。该应用通过Strava记录跑步里程,在世界著名路线上可视化用户的虚拟进度。

作者使用GeoNames开放数据集作为景点数据源,采用Python、Parquet和DuckDB构建数据处理管道。关键步骤包括:筛选有价值的地标类型(公园、历史遗迹、城堡等),利用Wikipedia链接作为知名度信号,过滤掉不重要的行政区划和小城镇。

作者强调了在项目中逐步引入新技术的学习策略,以及使用AI编程助手时保持对技术栈的掌控。最终将1300万条原始数据精简至72.5万条相关景点,为用户提供路线沿途的有趣地标信息,增强长期跑步动力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI编程工具能否替代人类的"品味"判断，以及如何在AI辅助开发中保持代码质量

不同观点：
• **无法完全外化观点**（trjordan, TimXare）：人类的知识和品味无法完全形式化写下来交给AI，"品味是你忘记写下的规范，加上你无法写下的部分"。调试系统比运行系统需要更多资源
• **品味可以训练观点**（timroman）：品味可以通过大量上下文积累训练出来，当积累足够多的项目规范（如100个）时，AI就能做得很好。Rick Rubin的例子证明这是可训练的技能
• **AI作为辅助工具观点**（ChrisMarshallNY, tuo-lei）：AI在辅助角色中表现良好但需要人类监督。实践中是"AI生成200行代码，人类保留80行"——选择哪80行无法测试
• **测试的局限性**（layer8, a_c）：单元测试无法覆盖所有输入和状态，测试只能确保"不出错"而非"做对"，无法保证有用和令人愉悦

补充讨论：有人提到可以用linters等工具约束、通过工作流中的治理环节来体现品味，但这些都是部分解决方案。核心争议在于品味的可形式化程度。

48657049.article_content:
I’m building
In the Long Run
where runners do
virtual
runs on famous routes around the world. The app tallies up your Strava mileage and plots your total distance as progress against country- or continent-spanning routes. The intention is to provide long-term inspiration and motivation; life is a marathon, not a sprint. You can have a bad month or season but still make progress on your virtual traversal of the world.
The app shows your progress on interactive maps, which lets users do some exploring of their own. But I had long wanted to enrich the maps with interesting sights or historical sites. For routes I was familiar with I could build such lists myself but that doesn’t scale to routes spanning countries I am not familiar with. So I set out to find a data source for points of interest that I could build a pipeline off. Along the way I wrestled with taste and biases, and fought a hallucinating llm. I initially thought AI would be the feature, but it ended up merely in a supporting role alongside other signals and data processing mainstays.
Dataset and toolset
#
GeoNames
was an obvious starting point, an extensive data source with locations, categories and links. The full data set can be downloaded and has a Creative Commons licence. So with my friend Claude I set about building a pipeline to go from the raw dumps to serving relevant points of interest to users of
In the Long Run
.
We used Python as the programming language (had good library support for the tasks at hand), stored processed data locally as Apache Parquet files and used DuckDB as the query layer.
1
This was my first time using both Parquet and DuckDB but the ergonomics of both felt good and Claude introduced me to their features step by step (and most of the DuckDB work was SQL that I am very familiar with). In general I find adding one or two new tools or technologies to a project is the best way to learn. If the entire stack is new to you the learning curve will be too steep and it might put you off the project entirely. AI coding agents change this calculus somewhat, but even then I find having a handle on
most
of the technologies being used lets me steer the agent better and make informed decisions instead of blindly following its lead.
Point of interest feature screenshot for a runner on Route 66 near Springfield, Illinois.
I built a project plan with Claude before starting the implementation, outlining the different steps of the pipeline and feature work. As we went along we then built a spec/plan for each step that we could iterate on as we learned more from earlier work. This also meant I could start new agent sessions for each milestone. Condensing results from the previous milestones into short context and instructions for the next step gets you faster and better responses (I find big contexts quickly degrade the quality of agent work).
Notability and notable biases
#
To begin with we downloaded and unzipped all the
required files from Geonames
and set up gitignores for the data files as most are too large to be version controlled.
The first step of processing was joining the downloaded files on the relevant columns and filtering out rows that were not useful for our purposes. For instance we excluded administrative divisions: countries, states, regions etc. We also selected specific feature codes that we thought would be most interesting: parks, historic sites, castles, monuments, mountains, etc.
2
Finally we added a population filter on populated places and an elevation filter on mountains. I’m sure this led to some false negatives, but we wanted a rough first draft.
Somewhat unintuitively the
alternateNames.txt
Geonames dataset includes Wikipedia links (where
isolanguage=link
and
alternate_name like %en.wikipedia.org%
, this usecase feels bolted on to their schema after the fact but it is very helpful data to have). We used this as a notoriety/relevance signal, and it also provided texts that we could build blurbs from as Wikipedia summaries also have a Creative Commons licence.
We built a basic sanity check for this pipeline step that helped us verify we weren’t skipping notable landmarks, this let us tweak some of the filtering. For instance, the first draft pulled in the Australian rural locality
Stonehenge
but not the prehistoric megalithic structure (its more famous namesake). When working in English you also want to make sure you pull in the relevant alternate names / languages and use the relevant Wikipedia URL as a cross reference (GeoNames stores the canonical name in the local language).
The final result of this step was a parquet file with around 725 thousand rows for points of interest globally. A significant reduction from the 13 million in the full original set we started out with.
Populated places are the bulk of the Geonames dataset. But we don't want the points of interest to just show every town, village and hamlet on the way.

主要讨论点：人们为何反感AI技术

不同观点：

• **权力与资源集中派**：AI加剧财富和权力向少数人集中，威胁就业但未创造等量新岗位，失业者难以转型（everdrive, coldtea, dayofthedaleks）

• **质量与诚意质疑派**：AI等同于低质量和敷衍，代表"我不在乎你所以用AI应付"的态度；输出充斥谎言、平庸内容和虚假工作，难以辨别真伪（nancyminusone, QuadrupleA, sys_64738）

• **实际应用批判派**：技术理论潜力无关紧要，关键看实际用途——AI被用于垃圾邮件、舆论操控、版权侵犯和网络污染（bariumbitmap, coldtea）

• **强制推广反感派**：用户明确表示不想要AI功能，但产品仍强行添加；体现硅谷"我们比你懂"的傲慢态度（coldtea, jjulius）

• **温和派/使用者**：40%的人支持或不在乎AI，高中师生普遍在用；HN上许多人日常工作依赖LLM（orangedog, voidUpdate）

补充讨论：
有从业者指出AI催生新型欺诈者（经理用Claude生成无意义回复）；网络环境恶化（反爬虫导致浏览器限制、去匿名化趋势）；硬件价格上涨；有人讽刺"如果不是泡沫，为什么长得像泡沫"。

data.author: leonagano
data.article_summary: 这是一份圣保罗市的创业公司目录，列出了154家初创企业和662个职位空缺。涵盖领域包括金融科技（Nubank、Creditas等数字银行和支付公司）、电商物流（iFood、Loggi配送平台）、房地产科技（Loft、QuintoAndar）、医疗健康（Sami、Alice）、人力资源（Gupy招聘）、教育科技和保险科技等。企业发展阶段从早期到上市公司不等，展示了巴西科技创业生态的多样性和活力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于某个展示创业公司地理分布的地图项目的讨论

不同观点：
• **地理聚集现象分析**（rescbr）：创业公司像其他白领公司一样聚集在历史商业区，办公地点选择反映创始人个性——老城区租金便宜但建筑陈旧；Paulista大道交通文化便利；Pinheiros曾是美食区但已过度士绅化失去灵魂；Faria Lima是核心金融区；Vila Olímpia是次级金融区，建筑高端但租金相对便宜

• **相似项目对比**：有人提到德国类似网站germantechjobs.de（staernid）和StartupMap（denysjw），认为功能相似但侧重点不同

• **数据完整性质疑**（khurs）：询问数据来源和完整性，对地理聚集结论的准确性表示关注

• **应用场景探讨**（bigjick）：询问主要用途是否为开发者提供工作机会

补充讨论：有用户表达复制意愿（anitil想为悉尼做类似项目并询问数据获取方式），也有呼吁为其他地区（如印度）开发类似版本的需求（dhruv3006）。K0balt的评论是双关玩笑（Brazilian/brazillion）。整体氛围积极，但缺乏对项目具体功能和价值的深入讨论。

data.title: Apple just Increased Prices: here’s what’s changed
data.author: jaimebuelta
data.article_summary: 苹果今日大幅提价多条产品线，平均涨幅269美元。Mac Studio (M3 Ultra)涨价最高达1300美元，MacBook Pro涨300美元，iPad Pro涨200美元。CEO Tim Cook将此归咎于内存和存储芯片成本飙升，称这是"百年一遇"的供应短缺。苹果历来自行吸收成本波动，此次转嫁给消费者标志着策略重大转变。iPhone、AirPods和配件未受影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：苹果产品大幅涨价及其影响

不同观点：
• 认可苹果性价比的观点：enmerk4r指出苹果近年来通过垂直整合已成为顶级硬件中性价比最高的选择，涨价是供应链问题的警示信号，并非苹果本身的问题

• 受涨价直接影响的用户：jaimebuelta的目标配置涨价1000美元；codazoda的Mac Studio从2600美元涨至3400美元（涨幅30%），打乱了储蓄计划，原本预计2027年涨价但苹果提前行动

• 市场替代方案浮现：codazoda表示涨价使带GPU的PC更具吸引力，特别是对运行本地AI模型的需求而言

• 及时购买者：cmdrmac庆幸在涨价前几天下单

• 质疑数据准确性：Thomaschaaf对"平均涨价269.23美元"的计算方法提出疑问

• 悲观论断：DiabloD3认为这是苹果变相承认Mac已死

补充讨论：评论中提到了相关讨论链接，显示这是一个广泛关注的话题。整体氛围偏负面，多数用户对涨价幅度表示不满，部分用户开始考虑转向竞品。

Apple Just Increased Prices: Here's What's Changed
Thursday June 25, 2026 5:44 am PDT
by
Hartley Charlton
Apple today dramatically increased device prices across multiple product lines.
After temporarily taking it
down earlier today
, Apple's online store is back up with a series of product price increases. The changes are as follows:
HomePod mini
: $129, up from $99 (+$30)
HomePod
: $349, up from $299 (+$50)
Apple TV
: $199, up from $129 (+$70)
iPad Air
: $749, up from $599 (+$150)
iPad Pro
: $1,199, up from $999 (+$200)
MacBook Neo
: $699, up from $599 (+$100)
MacBook Air
: $1,299, up from $1,099 (+$200)
MacBook Pro
: $1,999 up from $1,699 (+$300)
iMac
: $1,499, up from $1,299 (+$200)
Mac mini (M4 Pro)
: $1,599, up from $1,399 (+$200)
Mac Studio (M4 Max)
: $2,499, up from $1,999 (+$500)
Mac Studio (M3 Ultra)
: $5,299, up from $3,999 (+$1,300)
Vision Pro
: $3,699, up from $3,499 (+$200)
The average price increase is $269.23. The iPhone, AirPods,
Studio Display
, and accessories such as the
Apple Pencil
are seemingly the only unaffected product lines.
It is also of note that the 256GB
Mac mini
is now available again, but for $799. This is a $200 increase over when it was available before temporarily disappearing from the lineup earlier this year.
Last week, Apple announced that it was preparing to raise prices across its product lineup, with

DATABASES
The database that refused to die: How Postgres survived its own creators
From academic toss-aside to cloud substrate
Joab Jackson
Joab
Jackson
Published
mon 22 Jun 2026 // 18:43 UTC
FEATURE
Today Postgres is one of the most widely used database systems, but its launch and subsequent development were inauspicious to say the least.
If it weren’t for a league of exceptionally devoted open source contributors, it probably would be another forgotten also-ran just like Ingres, the database system on which it was based (“Postgres” was shorthand for “Post-Ingres”).
The creator of both systems,
Michael Stonebraker
, is perhaps the preeminent database pioneer in the field.
Earlier this month,
he spoke at
PGDay
, a conference in Boston hosted by the U.S. PostgreSQL Association, where he detailed the complicated history of the open source database system, which actually existed long before the term "open source" was even uttered.
REG AD
REG AD
In a sense, “Postgres is the epitome of open source software, because it doesn't belong to anybody. It was picked up by this team of programmers without any specific affiliation,” Stonebraker said.
Stonebraker essentially abandoned Postgres in the mid-1990s. But instead of fading into obscurity, the codebase was salvaged by a fiercely-dedicated volunteer community that bolted on standard SQL while preserving Stonebraker’s revolutionary extensible architecture.
Three decades later, this stubbornly-independent database has become the bedrock of modern cloud infrastructure.
Data should be relational
When it comes to relational database systems,
British computer scientist and then-IBM employee
Ted Codd got the ball rolling in 1970. A database is where you store your data so it can be queried in a predictable way. A database system is the software that manages the database (don’t confuse the two).
That year, Codd
decreed that all data
should be stored in tables and accessed using a high-level query language. IBM implemented Codd’s idea in System R, and created SQL as the query language. The results were eventually rolled into IBM's DB2.
Stonebraker, then an assistant professor at UC Berkeley, also implemented Codd’s ideas. Stonebraker and his team of grad students created not only a working prototype, but a full-scale implementation – he later cofounded a startup, Relational Technology, to sell Ingres commercially. Ingres did not use SQL, but instead employed another query language, QUEL (Query Language), although the fundamentals were similar.
MORE CONTEXT
The new database world according to Google: Inexact queries and AI in everything
SQL Server may be too lucrative for Microsoft to ditch, but too legacy to love
PostgreSQL backup tool gets some backup of its own after sole maintainer sounds alarm
IBM asks DBAs to trust AI to act on their behalf
A relatively primitive version of Ingres was even released gratis for academic research. But by the early 1980s, Stonebraker had “pushed the code off a cliff” and started building something new.
REG AD
Thus,
Postgres
was born.
Beyond Ingres: Postgres
At the time, Stonebraker explained, the business world was pushing for databases to hold additional data types beyond the integers, floats, and character strings required for basic business accounting. There was complicated CAD data and GIS data, with multiple data points that needed to be stored and reasoned against.
It was clear to Stonebraker and his colleagues that the ideal database system needed to be extended with more data types, user-defined data types, user-defined operators, and user-defined functions.
Adding more data types and such might seem simple enough, but the “devil is in the details,” he noted. “You need to be able to teach the query optimizer about new types, and that's not exactly easy.”  Commutative rules had to be worked out, and they had to be optimized.
This led to what was probably Postgres’ most successful feature: support for abstract data types (ADTs).
Stonebraker had other ambitions for Postgres as well. He also wanted to incorporate new work from Chris Date on
referential integrity,
which brought “semantic consistency between foreign keys and primary keys” to the relational model. He wanted to add in a rules engine, which would continually monitor for changes and make decisions based on those changes. Also, he wanted crash recovery.
The crash recovery and the rules engine never quite worked out, but the ADTs took root, and now most database systems support this extensibility, pretty much exactly like they were devised by Stonebraker and Co. in 1983.
REG AD
“We pretty much got it right,” he said. In fact, he reckons that his work on ADTs was probably the major reason he landed the Association for Computing Machinery’s
2014 A.M. Turing Award
.
